newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Elite rated hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Elite rated hold.

text.p: Israel's Elite Industries, a maker of coffee and chocolates, was lowered to a hold from a long-term buy by Bank Hapoalim's securities division in a report released on Sunday.

Hapoalim said the sharp drop in Elite's revenues in 1996, due to the sale of much of its European operation, would reverse this year and the company would enjoy improved gross margins. But it said that operating margins would not improve.

"The heavy competition in which the company finds itself (in the domestic market) will bring further high advertising and selling costs...that will lead to an erosion of operating margins," the bank said.
It estimated gross margins would rise to 24 percent in 1997 from 20.8 percent in 1996, while operating margins would remain unchanged at 4.0 percent.

Hapoalim forecast 1996 earnings per share of 0.75 shekel, rising to 0.95 shekel in 1997 and 1.64 shekels in 1998. The 1998 figure would be lifted by the expected sale of real estate held by the company, the report said.

"On the basis of these results, we estimate the value of Elite Industries at $220 million to $240 million (similar to our previous estimate), while the market value is about $248 million," Hapoalim said.
